title: Margins, EBITDA & Earnings Quality
description: Master how to evaluate profitability depth using margin analysis, EBITDA adjustments, and earnings quality signals.

interactions.prompt: A retailer has 40% gross margin but only 8% operating margin. What does the 32-point gap most likely indicate?

options.text: High SG&A spending relative to revenue
Excessive cost of goods sold
Unusually low tax rates inflating profit
Strong pricing power eroding over time

interactions.teachingPreamble: Gross margin measures profitability after direct costs (COGS), while operating margin subtracts all operating expenses like SG&A, R&D, and depreciation. A large gap between the two reveals how much overhead is consuming your gross profit - common in retail chains with heavy store costs and marketing spend.

interactions.prompt: Peloton FY2022: Revenue $3.58B (down 11%), Gross Margin 19.2% (was 35.4%), Operating Margin -68.7%, EBITDA Margin -52.1%. What is the most critical signal?

options.text: Revenue decline is the primary concern
Gross margin collapse shows broken unit economics
Negative EBITDA suggests only a cash flow timing issue
Operating losses are normal for growth companies

interactions.prompt: Why do analysts often prefer EBITDA over net income when comparing companies across different countries and capital structures?

options.text: EBITDA includes all cash and non-cash items
It removes effects of financing, taxes, and depreciation policies
EBITDA is an official GAAP metric with strict rules
It always equals operating cash flow

interactions.teachingPreamble: EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation & Amortization) strips out financing decisions (interest), tax jurisdictions, and accounting choices around asset depreciation. This makes it useful for apples-to-apples comparisons - for example, comparing a debt-heavy LBO target in Germany with an equity-funded competitor in the U.S.

interactions.prompt: When a company's net income grows faster than its operating cash flow for multiple years, analysts should investigate ____ quality.

options.text: Earnings
Revenue
Dividend
Asset

interactions.prompt: You're evaluating two acquisition targets. Company A: 45% gross margin, 20% operating margin, stable. Company B: 60% gross margin, 12% operating margin, growing fast. Budget allows only one. Which do you choose?

options.text: Company A - proven operational efficiency with strong flow-through
Company B - higher gross margin means more room to optimize operations
Neither - the operating margin gap in B is a red flag
Delay decision until both show identical margin profiles

interactions.prompt: A software firm reports $200M revenue, $160M cash collected, and $40M in unbilled receivables recognized under ASC 606. What earnings quality concern does this raise?

options.text: None - ASC 606 requires recognizing revenue at contract signing
Aggressive revenue recognition may be front-loading future periods
The $40M gap proves fraud is occurring
Unbilled receivables only matter for manufacturing firms

interactions.teachingPreamble: Earnings quality measures how well reported profits reflect actual economic performance. Key red flags include: net income consistently exceeding operating cash flow, growing accruals (like unbilled receivables), frequent 'one-time' adjustments, and aggressive revenue recognition under ASC 606 where performance obligations may be debatable.

interactions.prompt: Rank these earnings quality warning signs from most severe (first) to least severe when evaluating a potential investment in a mid-cap industrial company.

options.text: Operating cash flow trails net income for 4 consecutive years
Company changed depreciation method, boosting EPS by 3%
Accounts receivable growing 2x faster than revenue growth
Three consecutive years of large 'non-recurring' restructuring charges

interactions.prompt: You just learned the industrial company from your analysis has announced it will begin capitalizing $50M of previously expensed R&D costs, boosting operating income by 15%. How does this change your assessment?

options.text: Positive - higher operating income means improved profitability
Neutral - this is a standard accounting update with no real impact
Concerning - it artificially inflates margins without changing cash flows
Positive - capitalized R&D always signals stronger innovation investment

interactions.priorContext: Previously you identified multiple earnings quality red flags at this industrial company including persistent cash flow shortfalls and fast-growing receivables. Now management has made an accounting policy change that further boosts reported earnings without any operational improvement.
